context_spans.label: G_n = Q x R^n with closed embeddings, G = colim G_n with the colimit topology, the set U with |x_j| < |cos(j x_0)|, and the V + V contradiction

standard_prerequisites: Context span 6879-6887: G_n = Q x R^n as a topological group with the Euclidean topology, closed embeddings G_n -> G_{n+1} appending a zero; G = colim G_n with the colimit topology (U open iff G_n cap U open for all n); the claim is that this is not a topological group

Context span 6889-6909: the set U = {(x_0, x_1, ...) : |x_j| < |cos(j x_0)| for j > 0}; since j x_0 is never an integral multiple of pi/2 (pi irrational) it is easy to show U cap G_n is open; if the colimit topology made G a topological group there would be an open neighbourhood V of 0 with V + V subset U; then for every j >= 0 some epsilon_j > 0 has (0, ..., 0, x_j, 0, ...) in V for |x_j| < epsilon_j; V + V subset U would force (x_0, 0, ..., 0, x_j, 0, ...) in U for |x_0| < epsilon_0 and |x_j| < epsilon_j; taking j with j epsilon_0 > pi/2 and x_0 in Q with |cos(j x_0)| < epsilon_j gives |cos(j x_0)| < |x_j| < epsilon_j, contradicting membership in U
core_obligations: The colimit topology on G makes all the inclusions G_n -> G continuous and U open in G (context: U cap G_n open for all n)
Addition is not continuous for this topology: the context derives a contradiction from any neighbourhood V of 0 with V + V subset U using the cos(j x_0) windows

Hence the colimit in topological spaces (which has this topology) carries a different structure from the colimit in topological groups (where continuity of addition would force a finer topology); the two colimits differ
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the system G_n and the colimit topology from the context
Recall the context open set U and the V + V contradiction
Conclude the two categorical colimits disagree
